At the end of subtitle C of title XXVIII, 
add the following new section: 
SEC. 28 ll. PROHIBITION ON USE OF AUTO-
MATED SPEED ENFORCEMENT CAM-
ERAS ON MILITARY INSTALLATIONS. 
Section 2661 of title 10, United States Code, 
is amended by inserting at the end the fol-
lowing new subsection: 
‘‘(e) P
ROHIBITION ON USE OF AUTOMATED 
SPEED ENFORCEMENT CAMERAS.—(1) Notwith-
standing any other provision of law, no Fed-
eral funds may be used by the Secretary of 
Defense to purchase, install, operate, main-
tain, or contract for the operation of an 
automated speed enforcement camera sys-
tem on a military installation. 
‘‘(2) By not later than 180 days after the 
date of the enactment of this subsection, the 
Secretary shall ensure that any automated 
speed enforcement camera system in oper-
ation on a military installation as of the 
date of the enactment of this section is de-
commissioned and removed. 
‘‘(3) Nothing in this subsection may be con-
strued to— 
‘‘(A) limit the authority of an installation 
commander to enforce posted speed limits on 
the military installation under the jurisdic-
tion of the commander through means other 
than automated speed enforcement cameras; 
or 
‘‘(B) affect the use of any camera or photo-
graphic device for purposes of security, ac-
cess control, force protection, or criminal in-
vestigation, so long as such camera or photo-
graphic device is not primarily used for 
speed enforcement. 
‘‘(4) In this subsection: 
‘‘(A) The term ‘automated speed enforce-
ment camera system’ means any system that 
uses a photographic, video, or other elec-
tronic device to— 
‘‘(i) automatically detect and record the 
speed of a motor vehicle; and 
‘‘(ii) generate a record of any vehicle trav-
eling in excess of a posted speed limit. 
‘‘(B) The term ‘military installation’ has 
the meaning given such term in section 2801 
of this title.’’.

§2801. Scope of chapter; definitions (a) The term "military construction" as used in this chapter or any other provision of law includes any construction, development, conversion, or extension of any kind carried out with respect to a military installation, whether to satisfy temporary or permanent requirements, or any acquisition of land or construction of a defense access road (as described in section 210 of title 23). (b) A military construction project includes all military construction work, or any contribution authorized by this chapter, necessary to produce a complete and usable facility or a complete and usable improvement to an existing facility (or to produce such portion of a complete and usable facility or improvement as is specifically authorized by law). (c) In this chapter and chapter 173 of this title: (1) The term "appropriate committees of Congress" means the congressional defense committees and, with respect to any project to be carried out by, or for the use of, an intelligence component of the Department of Defense, the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives and the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate. (2) The term "facility" means a building, structure, or other improvement to real property. (3) The term "life-cycle cost-effective", with respect to a project, product, or measure, means that the sum of the present values of investment costs, capital costs, installation costs, energy costs, operating costs, maintenance costs, and replacement costs, as estimated for the lifetime of the project, product, or measure, does not exceed the base case (current or standard) for the practice, product, or measure. (4) The term "military installation" means a base, camp, post, station, yard, center, or other activity under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of a military department or, in the case of an activity in a foreign country, under the operational control of the Secretary of a military department or the Secretary of Defense, without regard to the duration of operational control. (5) The term "Secretary concerned" includes the Secretary of Defense with respect to matters concerning the Defense Agencies. (d) This chapter (other than sections 2830, 1 2835, and 2836 of this chapter) does not apply to the Coast Guard or to civil works projects of the Army Corps of Engineers.

action.short_description: Creating a qualified investor security-clearance pilot for defense technology
action.compact_description: The failed amendment would require a pilot but retain discretionary participation, lawful need-to-know, facility-or-alternative security and other safeguards. No foreign cleared professional, personal-gain use or preferred Federal award is authorized. Reports begin1yearfromenactment; authority sunsets5yearsfromenactment unless reauthorized. Whole technology-versus-investment/security membership remains unaccepted.
action.meaning:
The House rejected exact PartA30to H.R.8800, the national-security investor personnel-clearance pilot. The whole proposed section would require the Secretary, acting through DCSA, to establish a pilot supporting investment in qualifying national-security technology companies. Rejection did not add this section to the bill, grant a clearance, prefer a particular investor or certify a company.
Establishment SHALL occur under the proposal, while participation approval and investor sponsorship are discretionary and subject to Secretary approval. A sponsored clearance could be maintained independently of a specific Federal contract only while the investor remains eligible. Access to classified information requires a LAWFUL NEED-TO-KNOW and applicable security procedures; the pilot is not unrestricted classified access or a waiver of all clearance requirements. Authorized uses are solely the listed diligence, development/scaling/commercialization, Federal engagement, company support and authorization-assistance purposes.
An eligible investor must be a UnitedStatesperson/entity providing the listed investment support, NOT owned, controlled or influenced by a foreign person, with the specified relevant technology history and additional Secretary-prescribed requirements. Covered companies are USsmallbusinessconcerns under the incorporated632definition or Secretary-designated medium businesses developing/producing/commercializing relevant technology/products/services. The retained632(a)(1)unit supplies only the general independently-owned/operated and not-dominant definition; other SBA size/program rules, foreign-person determinations and individual eligibility are not certified. Investor representatives qualify as cleared professionals only after being granted a clearance under the section. No foreign person may serve in that role.
Each participating investor must maintain a FACILITY CLEARANCE OR Secretary-approved ALTERNATIVE SECURITY ARRANGEMENT, and comply with industrial-security, insider-threat and reporting requirements. The Secretary MAY suspend or revoke participation for security violations or foreign-ownership/control/influence concerns. Classified access may not be used for personal financial gain, securities trading, market manipulation or unrelated purposes. Those printed restrictions coexist with the listed investment-support purposes; this candidate does not adjudicate permissible profit or an individual transaction. Participation provides NO PREFERENCE in Federal contracts, grants or assistance. No numerical participation cap is imposed by this section; that is not automatic approval or guaranteed funding.
The first congressional-defense-committee report would be due one year AFTER ENACTMENT and annually thereafter, describing participation, clearances, supported companies, measured impacts, incidents/concerns and recommendations. Required impact reporting is not proof of actual innovation, manufacturing or security results. Authority under this section terminates five years AFTER ENACTMENT unless reauthorized by law; the text does not revoke every clearance authorized under other law. Current clearance regulations, security implementation and individual company/investor classifications remain uninspected.
An Aye would support this whole conditional pilot; a No opposes it without a component-specific position. Infrastructure/Technology membership is an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal based on expressly supporting national-security technology development and commercialization through qualified security-clearance sponsorship. A competing boundary treats the whole choice as investment/security-personnel administration. Independent whole-version, security/baseline and taxonomy review is required. No clearance award, unrestricted disclosure, preferred contract, actual investment/innovation/security result, wrongdoing, motive or enactment is inferred.
